title: The /lean4:refactor workflow: strategy-level proof simplification behind a per-batch diagnostic gate
intent: Prescribe a seven-step process for strategy-level proof simplification — audit for long proofs and thin definition APIs, search mathlib, plan with measured impact, approve per batch, apply each edit behind a diagnostic gate that reverts on any new diagnostic or sorry increase, verify through lake lean/lake build, then report — while never changing theorem statements or introducing axioms.

children.name: audit
children.statement: Read target proofs, identify repeated patterns, long proofs (>30 lines), hand-rolled arguments, case splits replaceable by congr/EqOn/EventuallyEq, thin definition APIs
children.closed_by: read-only scan; produces one opportunity per finding for the Search step

children.name: search
children.statement: For each opportunity, search mathlib via the LSP-first protocol; --search=quick is up to 2 LSP queries per opportunity, --search=full up to 5 with module exploration
children.closed_by: the bounded LSP query budget per opportunity

children.name: plan
children.statement: Present findings with estimated impact (Strategy Improvements, Helper Extraction, and an Estimated Impact block: Lines before: N → after: ~N | Helpers: N | New mathlib lemmas: N)
children.closed_by: the plan's Estimated Impact block, which states the line-count reduction before any edit

children.name: approval
children.statement: Ask before each batch (--dry-run stops here); a batch groups opportunities within a single proof or closely related proofs; prompt: Apply batch N (M changes)? [yes / skip / stop]
children.closed_by: the user's yes/skip/stop answer to the per-batch prompt

children.name: apply
children.statement: Edit files, verify with lean_diagnostic_messages after each batch; revert batch on any new diagnostic or sorry increase
children.closed_by: lean_diagnostic_messages clean and no sorry increase after the batch

children.name: verify
children.statement: lake lean <file> file gate (run from project root; it builds the file's imports first, so a cross-file batch cannot false-fail against a stale .olean); lake build project gate if multi-file; if final gate fails, revert all batches applied in this session
children.closed_by: the lake lean file gate or lake build project gate

children.name: report
children.statement: Summarize changes applied, helpers extracted, line count delta
children.closed_by: the report summary itself, which states the line-count delta

applicability.goal_shape: A set of already-compiling proofs (no sorries, no build errors) whose simplification is strategy-level rather than tactic-level: long proofs (>30 lines), repeated patterns, hand-rolled arguments replaceable by congr/EqOn/EventuallyEq or a mathlib lemma, or definitions with a thin API.
applicability.use_when: The proofs compile and the change preserves statements and adds no axioms; a mathlib lemma or a congr/EqOn/EventuallyEq rewrite is likely to replace hand-rolled reasoning; a helper is reused within a file and should be lifted to a private theorem.
applicability.avoid_when: The target has sorries or build errors (the command refuses); the change would alter a theorem statement or needs axiom/assumption hygiene (those are reported, or sent to the axiom-eliminator, not applied here); the cleanup is purely local tactic-level (that is /lean4:golf, which escalates to this command only for multi-file or strategy-level changes).

claims.claim: The ## Actions section (lines 58-75) specifies seven ordered steps — Audit, Search, Plan, Approval, Apply, Verify, Report — and the Apply step (5) requires editing, then verifying with lean_diagnostic_messages after each batch and reverting the batch on any new diagnostic or sorry increase.

Verification is two-tier: lake lean <file> runs from the project root and builds the file's imports first so a cross-file batch cannot false-fail against a stale .olean, lake build is the project gate for multi-file changes, and a final-gate failure reverts all batches applied in the session (line 74).
The command declares itself a mutating command that 'Does not change theorem statements, introduce axioms, or create commits' (line 11).

The helper-scope defaults (line 79) fix the extraction decision by reuse count: single use inside one proof → local have/local helper, reused within one file → private theorem, public/non-private → only with explicit user approval or a clear existing API reason.

metrics.how_counted: steps counted from the numbered list in refactor.md lines 60-75; the 30-line threshold and the 2/5 LSP-query budgets are the numbers the command states in lines 60-61; verification tiers are the lake lean file gate and the lake build project gate named in line 74

consequences: Every edit must pass two gates before it stands: a per-batch lean_diagnostic_messages check with no new diagnostic and no sorry increase, and a final lake lean (single file) or lake build (multi-file) gate; a failure reverts the batch, and a final-gate failure reverts the whole session. Helper extraction carries a scoping obligation: single use stays a local have, reuse within a file becomes a private theorem, and public visibility needs explicit approval. The command never changes theorem statements, introduces axioms, or creates commits, so statement-level changes are out of scope and are reported rather than applied. Failure modes: a cross-file batch verified only by lean_diagnostic_messages could false-fail against a stale .olean, which is why the file gate builds imports first; and a batch that reduces line count but breaks a proof is caught only by the sorry/diagnostic gate, not by the line-count delta.
